subject: Re: DPA redlines, order form pricing impact, and role split — decision needed
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@clearwave.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Nora Lin <nora.lin@clearwave.com>, outside-legal@clearwave.com
Date: 2026-09-09T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: DPA + order form: redlines and pricing impact

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the demo last week — ClearWave is keen to move forward. Our legal team attached a first-pass DPA redline (attached) and flagged two items that will affect commercial terms:

1) Processor/Controller role split — they want firm controller obligations for export approvals, which may require an order-form addendum.
2) Data residency guarantee — they asked for a UK/EU locality commitment for a subset of records; that seems like a pricing/hosting uplift.

Can you confirm Redwood's stance on:
- Whether the DPA redline is acceptable in principle or requires escalation to Privacy Counsel?
- High-level estimate of pricing uplift for a partial EU residency for ~10% of tokens and a dedicated KMS integration?

I've copied our outside counsel; they prefer to align on the DPA sooner than later. We attached the redline as ClearWave_DPA_redline_v1.docx.

High level ask: a short decision grid and an internal owner who can sign off on updates so we can keep our procurement timeline (target signature by end of September).

Appreciate a quick sync — Samir

--
Samir Patel
Head of Procurement, ClearWave Therapeutics
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@clearwave.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-09T12:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA + order form: redlines and pricing impact

Samir — thanks for the clear summary and the redline. We reviewed the document and routed it to our legal & privacy teams. Quick answers below, and proposed next steps.

Short answers:
- Escalation: Ben (cc'd) recommends a limited escalation — the redline contains a mix of acceptable edits and a few asks that require legal review (controller wording and residency commitment).
- Pricing uplift: I ran a quick ops estimate with Infra — partial EU residency (10% token routing + KMS integration) is likely a 12–18% uplift on the order form's compute+hosting line, plus a one-time integration fee (approx $6k). We'll formalize with numbers.

Next steps (proposed timeline):
- Today: Ben to confirm legal position on controller/processor language and whether to accept a transfer-addendum approach or a full substitution of SCCs.
- Tomorrow: Laura to draft a 1-page decision grid (options A/B/C) and updated order-form delta with the rough uplift so procurement can continue internal approvals.
- Tue 9/11 10:30am PT: 30-min call with ClearWave legal to align redlines and confirm evidence list.

I attached our canonical DPA clean copy (Redwood_DPA_clean.pdf) and added the order form draft to attachments. If that call works, I'll send a calendar invite.

Thanks — Marissa

--

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-09-09T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA + order form: redlines and pricing impact

Marissa / Samir — I looked through the ClearWave redlines. Summary and recommended path: 

Summary of concerning clauses:
- Controller obligations: ClearWave added unilateral notification timelines and approval gates for exports; this is broader than our standard DPA and would require product/infrastructure guarantees we don't typically commit to.
- Residency: Request for a hard EU data residency for a subset of data. Implementable via routing rules + dedicated node pool, but it is operationally measurable and should be priced.

Recommended path:
1) Accept most editorial and security edits in their redline.
2) For controller/processor split: propose language that preserves ClearWave's audit rights and export-notification SLA but ties approvals to documented evidence (SCCs + KMS logs). Offer a 30-day escalation window to PWG/privacy counsel rather than immediate clause replacement.
3) For residency: offer a Transfer Impact Addendum (TIA-style) in lieu of a global guarantee. The addendum will: 
   - Define the 10% workload scope
   - Specify routing to EU-hosted nodes and KMS integration
   - Quantify the uplift: "compute/hosting + 15%" and a one-time integration fee of $6,000.

I can draft the legal proposal language today. Marissa — please confirm you want me to:
- Draft the TIA + redline responses (I can deliver EOD)
- Join Tue 9/11 10:30am PT call to present the legal position

Ben

--
Ben Carter

Samir — thanks, Ben — that approach sounds right. Quick operational notes and the invite: 

- Decision owner: I'll act as deal owner for commercial signoff and procurement questions; Ben will handle legal redline responses and Laura will produce the decision grid and updated OrderForm_v3.xlsx with the uplift line.
- Calendar: I sent a calendar invite for Tue 9/11 10:30am PT (30 min) — invite includes a short agenda and a shared Drive link to the redline + our clean DPA.
- What we need from you ahead of the call: a short list (2–3 bullets) of the non-negotiable controller obligations and confirmation that the 10% residency scope is an approximate target. That will let Ben scope the TIA language.

If we can align on the TIA + pricing, we should be able to keep the signature target of end-September without further escalation.

Regards,
Marissa
